source_search_execution_summary.stop_reason: Max iterations reached (iteration_index=2, max_iterations=2). Evidence coverage is substantively sufficient: three distinct in-scope Salmonella outbreak events (cucumbers June 2024, backyard poultry May 2024, eggs May–July 2024) are each covered by at least one authoritative CDC or FDA source candidate with quantitative epidemiological data. iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Strong coverage across three confirmed in-scope outbreak events. Cucumber outbreak (June 2024): FDA page with 449 cases/31 states as of July 1 2024; CDC index and investigation update pages. Backyard poultry outbreak (May 2024): CDC index page with 470 cases/125 hospitalizations/1 death; CDC investigation update with illness date range through September 2024 (onset dates within target window); CDC media release May 23 2024; CIDRAP corroboration. Eggs/Milo's Poultry Farms (onset May 23 2024): CDC investigation page with 65–93 cases/9–12 states. FSIS.usda.gov (5 results) provides additional meat/poultry recall candidate sources. doh.wa.gov provides subnational Washington state data. All target fields have candidate evidence from at least one source per outbreak.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: High. Primary sources are cdc.gov and fda.gov official outbreak investigation pages — highest trust tier for US Salmonella surveillance. FSIS.usda.gov is authoritative for meat/poultry recalls. CIDRAP (cidrap.umn.edu) is a well-established academic public health news source that consistently cites official data. doh.wa.gov is a state government health department. News sources (abc7ny, allrecipes) cite named official agencies and are acceptable for corroboration. Out-of-scope pages (2025, 2026 CDC pages) were correctly flagged and rejected. The X/CDCgov tweet from iteration 1 was correctly flagged as unverified until the CDC investigation page (backyardpoultry-05-24) confirmed the 2024 date and figures.
